correctness.rationale: Kummer's theorem gives the valuation as the minimum borrow count. For \(N=p^s+p^t\), the only no-borrow lower indices are \(0,p^s,p^t,N\); the two proper nonzero possibilities are not divisible by \(m\) because \(p\) is a unit modulo \(m\). Hence every admissible lower index has at least one borrow. The explicit index \(k=mp^{t-1}\) has exactly one borrow because \(m<p\), including the adjacent-digit case \(s=t-1\). A fresh independent replay over 86 admissible small parameter quadruples confirmed both the minimum borrow count and the witness; this finite check is corroborative only.
residual_risks: No correctness defect is asserted; rejection is prior-implication/value based.

originality.rationale: A primary paper posted on 1 October 2026 proves the sharp universal row-by-row bound \(v_p(G(N;m))\le r_p(m)\) for every admissible row when \(p\nmid m\). Under the audited hypothesis \(p>m\), one has \(r_p(m)=1\), so that theorem supplies the entire upper bound for every row, not merely sparse rows. The remaining lower bound is the immediate Kummer no-borrow observation that a two-one-digit row has only \(0,p^s,p^t,N\) as no-borrow subdigits and none of the proper ones is selected. Thus the final equality is a direct special-case consequence of a strictly broader theorem plus the standard digit criterion.
